description: A multitrack sampler and sample oscillator, from one to sixteen tracks. It records, plays a selection out of the sample at a speed you set, tracks 1V per octave, and can cut the sample into slices

params.text: Sets the playback speed, -2x to +2x, default 1x; a negative speed plays the selection backwards and shows in red on the display
How much of the voltage at the speed input reaches the playback speed
How much of the voltage at the modulation input shifts the frequency of the module's own LFO
Sets the frequency of the module's own LFO
How much of the module's own LFO is added to the playback speed, which is what gives the scratching effect
Starts recording, and stops it when tapped again. Held with shift, what is recorded is added to the end of the sample; held with the command key the recording pauses
A tap starts playback from the beginning of the selection
A tap stops playback, and the next one carries on from where it stopped
Sets where in the sample the selection starts, which is where playback begins
Sets where in the sample the selection ends
Stretches the wave display vertically, and changes nothing about the sound
Shifts the playback in octaves, from -6 to +6
Sets a fade at the start and the end of playback to keep clicks out; it also sets the crossfade between the start of the sample and its reversed end, up to 1 second
Switched on, the sample plays only while the start gate is high
Switched on, the selection repeats; switched off, playback ends at the end of the selection
Sets the module's own LFO to unipolar, so it only ever adds to the playback speed
Inverts the shape of the module's own LFO
Switches the grid on and off. With the grid on the sample is divided into slices and the controls of the slice assembler are left out of use
Switched on, a random slice of the grid is picked at the end of each cycle; with the sample looping that gives an endless run of slices
A tap stores the current selection as a new slice
A tap loads the current stored slice as the playing selection
A tap replaces the current stored slice with the current selection
A tap deletes the current stored slice
A tap steps on to the next stored slice and loads it
A tap steps back to the previous stored slice and loads it
Balances the module's own signal against the incoming one while sound on sound is switched on
Switches on the yummer effect, which spreads the grains of the sample further apart in time
Sets the level of the yummer effect
Switches on the preview of the sound on sound mix while the module is not recording
Switches sound on sound on, so the incoming signal is mixed into what is recorded
Picks which of the stored slices is the current one
A tap picks a random stored slice
Steps the module's own LFO on to the next of its waves
Picks which slice of the grid is played
Switched on, the grid is divided at the peaks found in the sample rather than into equal parts
Switched on, a random stored slice is picked at the end of each cycle, which works while the grid is off
Switches recording over to CV data, which is written into the file at 100Hz and takes up to sixteen tracks

inputs.text: The signal to be recorded; the number of polyphonic channels arriving here sets how many tracks are recorded, up to sixteen
A pulse starts recording, and the next one stops it
A voltage shifting the frequency of the module's own LFO
A pitch voltage at 1V per octave, which plays the selection chromatically
A pulse starts playback from the beginning of the selection, and with the gated flag on a gate holds it
A pulse stops playback, and the next one carries on from where it stopped
A high voltage here switches the gated mode on
A voltage moving the start of the selection
A voltage moving the end of the selection
A pulse resets the phase of the module's own LFO
A clock here sets the frequency of the module's own LFO, in place of the rate knob
A voltage moving the depth of the module's own LFO
0-10V picks which slice of the grid is played
A pulse deletes the current stored slice
A pulse stores the current selection as a new slice
A pulse loads the current stored slice as the playing selection
A pulse replaces the current stored slice with the current selection
A pulse steps on to the next stored slice and loads it
A pulse steps back to the previous stored slice and loads it
A pulse picks a random stored slice
0-10V picks which of the stored slices is the current one
A voltage setting the balance between the module's own signal and the incoming one
A voltage moving the playback speed
A pulse activates the grid
A high voltage here switches looping on

outputs.text: The playback output, carrying one polyphonic channel for each track
A pulse each time playback reaches the end of the selection
The level of the sample as it plays, taken by an envelope follower
A ramp following the position of the playhead, across the current slice or across the whole sample

notes: recording can run in a pre-record mode holding up to 120 seconds, or straight to disk; playback always runs from memory, so how long a recording can be depends on the memory in the machine
right-clicking the wave display gives the editing commands: cut, copy, paste, delete, zero, invert, normalise, amplify, fades, trimming, and rendering the selection as the new sample
dragging the playhead with the alt key held moves it with granular playback, and dragging with shift held scratches it, the pitch following the speed of the drag
nothing plays until the sample buffer holds something: load a wav or aiff file from the menu, drop one onto the module, or record into it
dropping a folder loads every audio file in it, and a slice is made for each section that is appended
the Simpler Tape Control module drives playback speed from its AUX OUT, patched into the speed CV input
menu: DRAG & DROP files are appended — a dropped file is added to the end of the sample; switched off, a dropped file replaces it
REC to PLAY crossfade time — sets the crossfade between the recording buffer and the playing buffer, from 0 to 2 seconds
Open WAV or AIFF File... — loads a wav or aiff file as the sample
APPEND WAV or AIFF File... — adds a wav or aiff file to the end of the sample
Save WAV File... — writes the sample out as a wav file
Reload... — reads the original file back in, undoing edits made to the sample
Use AC wave draw style — draws the wave in the AC style, and changes nothing about the sound
GENERATE n EQUAL SLICES from SELECTION — on the wave display's menu, cuts the current selection into a set number of parts and adds them to the slice assembler
VISUALIZE STEREO, LEFT or RIGHT — on the wave display's menu, chooses which channels are drawn: Show STEREO, Show LEFT or Show RIGHT
TRIM Selection — on the wave display's menu, throws away everything outside the current selection
UN-TRIM Sample — on the wave display's menu, brings back what a trim threw away
RENDER Selection to Sample — on the wave display's menu, makes the current selection the whole sample
TIME DISPLAY MODE — sets what the time display shows: Show Sample Length Time, Show Selection Length Time, Show Selection Length Samples or Show Playhead Time
PRE-RECORD MODE — records for a set length rather than until it is stopped, with PRE-RECORD TIME in SECONDS: taking a value from 0.5 to 120 seconds

inputs.3: 1V per octave · continuous · one channel only
